# FLX-5042: the World names no vertical this engine ships

**Family:** numerics (the 5000 band)

A run builds its population from the vertical pack its World names in `spec.vertical`: the pack declares which attributes each simulated subject carries and which fields each signal's payload holds, and its alias table maps expose columns onto them. The FLUX schema leaves `spec.vertical` optional, so the FLUX reference validator (`python3 -m flux_spec.validate`) passes a World that names no vertical, or names one this engine does not ship. This engine then has nothing to build a subject from, even when a fidelity block declares every column. Add `vertical:` under the World's `spec`, naming one of the packs `fluxsim plugins` lists, for example `vertical: telco`. `fluxsim validate` refuses the bundle before anything runs, and `plan`, `run` and `expr` give the same refusal.

## Look it up offline

```console
$ fluxsim explain FLX-5042
```

Every code is listed in the [error index](./README.md).
